profile.headline: 254 million people live with chronic hepatitis B, and it is a vaccine-preventable cause of cirrhosis and liver cancer that treatment controls but does not cure.
profile.syndrome: Acute hepatitis, usually anicteric in children and symptomatic in adults, rarely fulminant. Chronicity depends almost entirely on the age at infection: about 90% of perinatal infections become chronic against under 5% of adult ones. Chronic infection moves through immune-tolerant, immune-active, inactive-carrier and reactivation phases towards cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma, which can arise without cirrhosis because the virus integrates.
profile.transmission: Perinatal, percutaneous and sexual. The infectious dose is very low and the virus survives on surfaces for days, which is why household and nosocomial transmission occur without an obvious exposure.
profile.reservoir: Humans; the genotypes trace human migration closely enough to be used as a marker of it.
profile.geography: Worldwide, with the highest prevalence in the WHO Western Pacific and African regions.
profile.diagnosis: HBsAg with anti-HBc, IgM anti-HBc for acute infection, HBeAg and anti-HBe, and HBV DNA for phase and treatment decisions; quantitative HBsAg and genotype in specialist practice.
profile.management: Nucleos(t)ide analogues — tenofovir or entecavir — suppress replication and reduce cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma, but rarely clear the infection, so treatment is usually lifelong. Pegylated interferon achieves functional cure in a minority. Surveillance for liver cancer continues regardless of suppression.
profile.prevention: Recombinant vaccine, with a birth dose within 24 hours the single most effective intervention; hepatitis B immune globulin with vaccine for infants of HBsAg-positive mothers; antiviral prophylaxis in pregnancy at high viral load; blood-donor screening and injection safety.
evidence: Among the best-established causal relationships in oncology: IARC Group 1, with cohort, molecular and vaccine-era incidence data all concordant. Taiwan's universal infant programme produced a measurable fall in childhood liver cancer.
